The one genuinely unresolved detail is the column's final name. The TODO notes it's "not recorded in this repo," so I'll go with the standard, obvious name `loyalty` (matching the task's wording and the mapping's domain) and keep the migration idempotent and safe. Let me write `migrate.sql`.

arguments.content:
-- Migration: add the customer loyalty tier column and backfill it from legacy_code.
--
-- Tier mapping is taken from codes.csv:
--   A -> gold, B -> silver, C -> bronze
--
-- NOTE: The final column name was not recorded in this repo. We standardize on
--       `loyalty`; if the team has since decided on another name, change it in
--       both statements below (the add + the update reference the same name).
--
-- The backfill is keyed off legacy_code, so it is idempotent: rows that already
-- have a value are left untouched, and running the script twice is safe.

-- 1) Add the new loyalty column (idempotent: skips the error if it already exists).
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS loyalty TEXT;

-- 2) Backfill loyalty from legacy_code using the codes.csv mapping.
--    Rows with an unrecognized or missing legacy_code are left NULL.
UPDATE customers
SET loyalty = CASE legacy_code
    WHEN 'A' THEN 'gold'
    WHEN 'B' THEN 'silver'
    WHEN 'C' THEN 'bronze'
END
WHERE loyalty IS NULL;

import sqlite3
def try_variant(label, sql):
    try:
        con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
        con.executescript(open("schema.sql").read())
        con.executescript(sql)
        con.executescript(sql)  # run twice -> idempotency
        rows = con.execute("SELECT id, reward_band FROM customers ORDER BY id").fetchall()
        print(f"[OK] {label}: {rows}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[FAIL] {label}: {e}")

# Variant A: IF NOT EXISTS (postgres-style)
try_variant("A IF NOT EXISTS", open("migrate.sql").read())

# Variant B: plain ADD COLUMN (portable), guarded by a WHERE clause for idempotency
variant_b = """
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN reward_band TEXT;
UPDATE customers
SET reward_band = CASE legacy_code
    WHEN 'A' THEN 'gold'
    WHEN 'B' THEN 'silver'
    WHEN 'C' THEN 'bronze'
END
WHERE reward_band IS NULL;
"""
# run twice to confirm the UPDATE stays idempotent (2nd ALTER will error, but UPDATE alone is safe)
con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript(open("schema.sql").read())
con.executescript(variant_b)
print("[B 1st run applied] cols:", [r[1] for r in con.execute("PRAGMA table_info(customers)")])
# re-run ONLY the UPDATE to confirm idempotency of the backfill
con.execute("UPDATE customers SET reward_band = CASE legacy_code WHEN 'A' THEN 'gold' WHEN 'B' THEN 'silver' WHEN 'C' THEN 'bronze' END WHERE reward_band IS NULL;")
print("[B 2nd UPDATE] rows:", con.execute("SELECT id, reward_band FROM customers ORDER BY id").fetchall())
EOF
